comment: The MS language should be made native, and grammatical errors should be polished.
requested_action: Perform a full native-English proofreading and grammatical polish pass over the manuscript.

comment: The abstract should be revised, and interesting findings should be included numerically.
requested_action: Rewrite the abstract and include key numerical findings (e.g., PR-AUC values, prevalences, spatial PR-AUC).

comment: It is recommended to write keywords alphabetically.
requested_action: Order the keywords alphabetically.

comment: The novelty of the work should be highlighted, and it should be stated what literature you have that has not been addressed so far.
requested_action: Add an explicit novelty statement and a knowledge-gap paragraph in the Introduction.

comment: In initial paragraph written on the topic water quality, it is recommended to use these articles: https://doi.org/10.1080/03067319.2024.2432583, https://doi.org/10.30955/gnj.005098, https://doi.org/10.1007/s13201-025-02661-5, https://doi.org/10.1007/s13201-026-02938-3, https://doi.org/10.1016/j.cep.2025.110160, https://doi.org/10.1080/00986445.2024.2445230
requested_action: Verify the listed references and cite the relevant verified ones in the water-quality opening paragraph.

comment: Some of the references are very old, dating back over 20 years. Please update them.
requested_action: Audit the reference list; retain foundational methodological references (Breiman, Friedman, Brier) with justification and add recent literature where directly relevant.
Verify each DOI; cite the verified, topic-relevant ones in the Introduction to fill the knowledge gap.

comment: Use the methodology materials of this article to improve the work: 10.1016/j.eswa.2025.130999
requested_action: Verify the DOI; if relevant, cite its methodology in the Methods and note any transferable methodological elements.

comment: Add the materials of this article to the topic in the discussion section. DOI: 10.1007/s10489-025-06839-x (prioritize uncertainty calibration to ensure model reliability in high-stakes screening, providing a cross-disciplinary methodological framework for robust decision-making under data uncertainty.)
requested_action: Verify the DOI; cite in the Discussion in the uncertainty-calibration context if relevant.

comment: Add to the discussion: DOI: 10.1080/17538947.2026.2646387 (address spatial heterogeneity and uncertainty in environmental modeling. Candidate 0's spatiotemporal correction logic provides a relevant parallel for the target's spatial validation and sensitivity analysis.)
requested_action: Verify the DOI; cite in the Discussion in the spatial-validation context if relevant.

comment: Add to the discussion: DOI: 10.1016/j.eswa.2026.131177 (address feature selection in high-dimensional datasets. LIMFS's focus on label interactions offers a methodological alternative for analyzing correlated hydrochemical constituents in multi-target groundwater risk assessments.)
requested_action: Verify the DOI; cite in the Discussion in the feature-selection context if relevant.

comment: Add to the discussion: DOI: 10.1016/j.patcog.2026.113096 (address small-sample uncertainty and class imbalance. The candidate's few-shot learning approach provides a methodological parallel to the target's challenge of modeling limited, clustered hydrochemical data.)
requested_action: Verify the DOI; cite in the Discussion in the small-sample/class-imbalance context if relevant.

comment: Add to the discussion: DOI: 10.1016/j.petsci.2026.05.001 (address data-limited subsurface environments and emphasize interpretability in well-based data analysis, providing a contextual bridge for handling geological heterogeneity and data uncertainty.)
requested_action: Verify the DOI; cite in the Discussion in the data-limited subsurface context if relevant.

comment: Add to the discussion: DOI: 10.1109/tifs.2025.3626979 (paper tackle the challenge of predictive modeling in highly imbalanced datasets where target events are rare, sharing a common logical goal of robust screening and detection frameworks.)
requested_action: Verify the DOI; cite in the Discussion in the imbalanced-data context if relevant.

comment: Add to the discussion: DOI: 10.1002/nag.70125 (address spatial variability and uncertainty in subsurface environments. Candidate 0's treatment of anisotropic spatial properties parallels the target's focus on spatial dependence and validation.)
requested_action: Verify the DOI; cite in the Discussion in the spatial-variability context if relevant.

comment: Add to the discussion: DOI: 10.1016/j.est.2025.118038 (address predictive bias and uncertainty. The candidate's bias-compensation framework in electrical systems offers a functional analogy for the target's leakage-control and validation logic in hydrochemical modeling.)
requested_action: Verify the DOI; cite in the Discussion in the bias/uncertainty context only if scientifically relevant.

comment: Use these articles in the introduction: DOI: 10.1038/s41467-026-68798-2
requested_action: Verify the DOI; cite in the Introduction if real and relevant.

comment: The abstract effectively sets up the problem but could be strengthened by explicitly stating the final recommendation for operational use (e.g., "We recommend using the EC-strict TDS model and the Tier 3 logistic regression for B as the primary screening tools").
requested_action: Add an explicit operational recommendation sentence to the abstract, derived from the validated results.

comment: The justification for using a TDS threshold of 750 mg/L, which is different from the WHO guideline of 1000 mg/L, should be more prominently stated as a study-specific screening choice rather than a regulatory limit to avoid confusion.
requested_action: State prominently in Methods and Discussion that all thresholds are study-specific precautionary screening choices, not regulatory limits; add explicit TDS rationale.

comment: Your tiered predictor design is excellent for operational relevance, but I wonder if you considered a fourth tier that also excludes coordinates to truly test if spatial information alone drives performance for some targets?
requested_action: Implement coordinate-excluded sensitivity variants (coordinate ablation) for all tiers and report them as sensitivity analyses.

comment: The spatial clustering using k-means on coordinates is practical, but could the resulting groups inadvertently separate wells that are hydrologically connected along a flow path, potentially overestimating the spatial penalty?
requested_action: Discuss this limitation explicitly in Methods/Discussion and frame spatial CV as a conservative transferability test.

comment: It's reassuring that you tested sensitivity to the number of spatial clusters (k=3-8), but the substantial spread for B and F (0.14-0.27) suggests that the spatial validation results for these targets are quite unstable, which should be emphasized more strongly in the discussion.
requested_action: Emphasize the k-sensitivity spread for B and F more strongly in Results/Discussion.

comment: For the EC-strict TDS model, achieving a PR-AUC of 0.975 without EC is impressive, but could you elaborate on what other predictors (e.g., Na, Cl, HCO3) are driving this performance, as this has practical implications for where lab resources should be focused?
requested_action: Report the principal non-EC predictors driving the EC-strict TDS model using the attribution outputs.

comment: The use of path-based (Saabas-style) feature attribution is appropriate for shallow trees, but given the complexity of gradient-boosted trees, have you considered validating these attributions with a more exact Shapley value approximation for a subset of models to ensure consistency?
requested_action: Resolve the SHAP/Saabas terminology issue completely and consider an exact-approximation consistency check or a clear statement of why it is not feasible here.

comment: The calibration curves for B and F show considerable bin-level uncertainty—does this uncertainty primarily stem from the small sample size, or is it indicative of a more fundamental lack of structure in the data that a different modeling approach might capture?
requested_action: Discuss the sources of calibration uncertainty (small sample size vs. weak structure) explicitly.

comment: Your framework is explicitly designed for "virtual screening" to prioritize confirmatory testing, but I'm curious how you envision a water manager actually using the probability cutoffs in Table 4, especially when they differ so widely (e.g., 0.29 for B vs. 0.43 for Cl).
requested_action: Add an explicit decision-support section explaining how a water manager should use target-specific cutoffs.

comment: The conclusion that NO3 is not suitable for modeling is well-supported by the data, but could you discuss whether a simpler, non-ML approach like a simple rule based on land use or proximity to agricultural areas might be more appropriate for nitrate risk in this region?
requested_action: Discuss the NO3 conclusion and the alternative of simple rule-based screening in the Discussion.

comment: The handling of below-detection-limit values using the detection-limit-divided-by-√2 convention is a common practice, but in a small dataset like this, have you tested the sensitivity of the results, particularly for F, to an alternative method like maximum likelihood estimation?
requested_action: Run a BDL substitution sensitivity analysis for F (and affected models) and justify the substitution choice; explain why a censored-model approach is or is not needed.

comment: The discussion of related work is thorough, but a more direct comparison of your PR-AUC results for Na and Cl (≈1.000) with those from the cited studies (e.g., Ansah-Narh et al., 2026) would help readers gauge the relative performance of your leakage-controlled approach.
requested_action: Add a cautious quantitative comparison with comparator studies where study designs permit.

comment: The manuscript is very detailed, but the reader would benefit from a single, simplified flowchart that focuses on the decision-making steps for an end-user (e.g., "Step 1: Choose target; Step 2: Select tier; Step 3: Apply cutoff; Step 4: Map priority").
requested_action: Add a simplified end-user decision flowchart to the main manuscript.

comment: Could you clarify the exact rationale for using the F2 score over the more common F1 score, specifically in the context of prioritizing wells for confirmatory testing, and why the choice of β=2 is optimal for your surveillance objective?
requested_action: Clarify that β=2 is an a priori surveillance preference (recall-weighted), not an optimized cost ratio; add a β sensitivity analysis (F1, F1.5, F2, F3).

comment: The limitation regarding the pooled selection of operational cutoffs from out-of-fold predictions is an important caveat, but would a fully nested selection procedure (within each outer fold) have led to overly conservative and less generalizable cutoffs?
requested_action: Implement fully nested operational-threshold selection and compare with the pooled approach; report both.

comment: It's interesting that for Na, the reduced-chemistry tier (Tier 2) slightly outperforms the full-chemistry tier (Tier 3) for gradient-boosted trees—does this suggest that adding more predictors introduces noise for this specific target, or is it a random effect of the small sample?
requested_action: Discuss the Tier 2 vs Tier 3 pattern for Na in terms of noise vs. small-sample variation.

comment: The GIS maps (Figure 7) are a valuable output, but I'd like to see a brief description of how the "low, moderate, high" screening priority classes were defined from the continuous probabilities, as this is a crucial step for translation to a decision support tool.
requested_action: Document the exact probability boundaries of the screening-priority classes in the main text.

comment: For F, where performance drops under spatial validation, could this spatial fragility be due to the fact that the five below-detection-limit wells are geographically clustered, thus reducing the information available to train the model for that specific spatial group?
requested_action: Test whether the five F BDL wells are geographically concentrated and whether substitution affects spatial results.

comment: The decision to not model NO3 due to only two exceedances is sound, but it would be beneficial to report its descriptive statistics and spatial distribution in the main text or a supplementary figure to justify this decision to the reader.
requested_action: Report NO3 descriptive statistics and spatial distribution (main text or supplementary figure).

comment: How do you recommend a user of this framework should interpret the Brier score, given that it is presented alongside PR-AUC, and what would be considered a "good" Brier score for a screening tool of this nature in environmental science?
requested_action: Provide Brier-score interpretation guidance: prevalence-dependent benchmarks, null-model Brier and Brier skill score.

comment: The paper is commendably transparent, but the data and code availability statement could be more explicit about whether the exact SQLite reproducibility database is also publicly accessible or only available upon request.
requested_action: Make the data/code availability statement explicit about the SQLite database and archived exports.

comment: A valuable future direction, which you briefly mention, would be to incorporate hydrogeological process models; I'd be interested to know if you think a simple lumped-parameter model of flow and transport could be integrated directly as a predictor to improve performance, especially for the spatially fragile targets like F.
requested_action: Address the lumped-parameter model idea explicitly in Future Work with a reasoned position.

comment: 'The model set comprised baseline, interpretable and nonlinear classifiers (Abdul-Wahab and Sunkari, 2026).'????? That is enough to REJECT this submission.
requested_action: Rephrase the model-set sentence to cite the primary methodological literature (Breiman 2001; Friedman 2001) instead of the project's own software record, and clarify what the software citation refers to.

comment: Incredible straightforward use of traditional logistic regression, RF and GB without any replication evidence and optimality approval, curve guarantees, error monitoring, early convergence, trapping...!!!!!!!!!!!!!
requested_action: Show that replication evidence exists (repeated nested CV, 25 folds, bootstrap CIs, dummy baselines) and make it highly visible; explain why exotic convergence guarantees are not applicable to the implemented estimators.

comment: No solid comparison with advanced approaches like https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s11053-022-10051-w / spatial distribution analysis / only relies on confusion matrix without any conducted matrix and lacks supportive metrics / lack of impact of bias of the data on the results / lack of referenced technical limitations…
requested_action: Demonstrate that the study already reports ROC-AUC, PR-AUC, recall, specificity, F1, F2, balanced accuracy, Brier, calibration, bootstrap CIs, spatial CV, and technical limitations; add a comparison with the cited spatial-distribution study where relevant.

comment: What about temporal variability of groundwater quality??? Due to time dependency of data, you need an updating procedure and dynamic filtering for sequential upcoming. This experiment doesn't provide a solution for a uniformly normalizing dynamic database across different factors. New approaches can be found at https://www.mdpi.com/1424-8220/24/4/1209, https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s00500-026-11232-y, … Overall, the robustness of the model to noise, missing data or malfunction is not discussed.
requested_action: Acknowledge explicitly that the study is cross-sectional; state that temporal/seasonal validation and model updating are out of scope for this dataset and describe them as required future work; do not add unsupported temporal analyses.

comment: Where is the claimed 'Leakage-controlled and spatially'???? This work basically doesn't have any spatial analysis and mapping.
requested_action: Show that the work already contains spatial clustering, spatial-group CV, spatial-penalty analysis, and GIS-ready priority maps; make these elements highly visible in the main manuscript.

comment: English requires substantial revision / many undefined acronyms and parameters at first appearance.
requested_action: Proofread the manuscript and define every acronym at first use.

comment: Trivial improper citations. Just as an example, the claimed citation to Sunkari et al., 2021 (L54, L57) or … obviously is REJECTED and it has been recognized much earlier than 2021.
requested_action: Verify the Sunkari et al. 2021 citation and all citations; correct any bibliographic errors.

comment: No embedded Fig/Tables/captions within the context.
requested_action: Ensure every figure and table is embedded in the main text with captions and in-text citations in logical order.

comment: Full opacity in terms of datasets, diversity, … randomization, unifications, time interval span, … opacity in binary risk-alert thresholds, spatial grouping strategy for cross-validation, spatial autocorrelation, selection of predictor variables, robustness to class imbalance, external or independent validation, ….
requested_action: Move all required methodological transparency details (dataset, thresholds, spatial grouping, CV, predictor selection, imbalance handling, external-validation status) into the main text.

comment: This work is more suitable for screening than definitive contamination prediction.
requested_action: Maintain and strengthen the screening-framework framing; ensure claim discipline throughout (screening probability ≠ contamination status).

comment: Unjustified conclusion.
requested_action: Reweigh conclusions to be strictly proportional to the evidence (target-specific screenability claims with explicit uncertainty).

comment: The precautionary thresholds used to define the binary outcomes require stronger justification. Please explain their scientific basis and, preferably, provide a sensitivity analysis using current drinking-water guideline values.
requested_action: Strengthen the threshold rationale and run a concentration-threshold sensitivity analysis using current guideline values where prevalence allows.

comment: The dataset includes only 81 wells, while some models use relatively large predictor sets. Please further discuss the risk of overfitting and the adequacy of the sample-to-predictor ratio, particularly for B and F.
requested_action: Add a small-sample/dimensionality audit: per-fold training sizes, positives per fold, sample-to-predictor ratios, regularization, fold variance, bootstrap uncertainty; discuss overfitting risk for B and F.

comment: The spatial clustering procedure requires clarification. The manuscript states that k-means clustering was applied using Haversine distances; please describe the exact implementation and justify why this approach is appropriate for geographic coordinates.
requested_action: Audit the clustering implementation; replace the incoherent Haversine/coordinate-mean k-means with projected Euclidean k-means or a great-circle medoid method and document the choice.

comment: Only three binary-valid spatial held-out folds appear to have been retained. Please explain how exclusion of spatial folds lacking both classes may influence the reported spatial PR-AUC and potentially bias estimates of geographic transferability.
requested_action: Report all spatial folds with n/pos/neg and metric definability; compute pooled spatial performance across all unique held-out wells; quantify any bias from single-class fold exclusions.

comment: The perfect or near-perfect PR-AUC values reported for Cl and TDS deserve more cautious interpretation, especially because EC is strongly related to dissolved ionic content. The possibility of proxy-driven discrimination should be discussed more explicitly.
requested_action: Discuss proxy-driven discrimination explicitly; report EC-ablation results for Cl and Na as well as the existing TDS EC-strict analysis.

comment: Operational probability thresholds were selected from pooled out-of-fold predictions rather than within the nested validation procedure. A fully nested threshold-selection strategy would provide a less optimistic estimate of operational sensitivity and specificity.
requested_action: Implement fully nested threshold selection within each outer fold and report unbiased operating estimates.

comment: The literature review should be updated by incorporating more recent studies on data-driven modelling, subsurface-water characterization, and monitoring approaches. The authors may consider relevant recent works such as 10.1016/j.icheatmasstransfer.2026.112082, 10.1016/j.pce.2026.104704, and 10.1016/j.advwatres.2026.105393 to strengthen the methodological context and discussion of the study.
requested_action: Verify these DOIs and update the literature where verified and relevant.

comment: The manuscript repeatedly refers to "SHAP-based" interpretation, while the implemented method is described as a Saabas-style path-based attribution approach. These methods are not equivalent; terminology should be corrected or exact TreeSHAP values should be calculated.
requested_action: Remove the term SHAP everywhere (manuscript, tables, figures, exports, database) unless exact TreeSHAP is implemented; use consistent path-based attribution terminology.

comment: Please clarify how false-positive and false-negative counts in Table 4 were calculated under repeated cross-validation and whether repeated predictions from the same well contributed more than once to these counts.
requested_action: Create well-level consolidated out-of-fold predictions (each well once, median OOF probability) for the principal decision table; label pooled counts explicitly as prediction-instance counts.

comment: The Results and Discussion sections contain substantial repetition, particularly regarding the superior screenability of Na, Cl and TDS and the weaker spatial performance of F. These sections could be shortened and made more analytical by reducing repeated numerical descriptions.
requested_action: Restructure Results and Discussion to remove repetition and make Discussion more analytical.
